people.name: Becky Bixby
people.bio: Research professor in the UNM Department of Biology who directs the university's Water Resources Program. An aquatic ecologist with a 2001 University of Michigan doctorate in biology, her research centers on periphyton ecology and biodiversity.
people.research_interests: Aquatic ecology; periphyton ecology and biodiversity

people.name: Anjali Mulchandani
people.bio: Assistant professor of civil, construction and environmental engineering at UNM, where she heads the Environmental Resource Sustainability group. Her research spans the water-energy nexus, harvesting water from the atmosphere, waste-to-energy technology and remediation, with an emphasis on science communication and community-needs research. Previously a Stanford postdoc; PhD from Arizona State.
people.research_interests: Environmental resource sustainability; water-energy nexus; atmospheric water harvesting; water quality; engineering education; science communication

people.name: Jingjing Wang
people.bio: Associate professor of economics at UNM working in environmental and natural-resource economics. She builds integrated and dynamic optimization models and econometric analyses of how policy and markets allocate water and other resources, including urban conservation, cross-sector water trading, livestock manure with bioenergy, and nitrogen in drylands.
people.research_interests: Water economics; nutrient management; renewable energy; climate change; integrated modelling
